transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, DC, I'm Dale Willman.
Former President Barack Obama was campaigning for Democratic candidates in Ohio and Michigan
Saturday, where he was greeted by large, loud crowds of supporters shouting, "Vote! Vote! Vote!"
Speaking in Detroit, Obama blamed President Trump's policies for the high prices facing consumers
right now, and he said it's time for something different. "People are so ready for something
new, so hungry for something better, so sick and tired of being sick and tired, that everywhere
you go it feels like change is in the air. And Michigan, that's what I'm feeling right now."
President Trump cast an early ballot in Florida Saturday before heading to Georgia to campaign
for Republicans. He also announced that automaker Audi will be building a new plant in the state,
committing $4.2 billion for the facility that will build 200,000 cars a year when it's completed
in the early 2030s. Ukraine says the satellite communication system Starlink and its Star Shield
technology is now fully functioning in that country again, and Piers Polina Litvinova reports from Kyiv.
In his video address, President Zelensky said the disruptions were over at night and by the
morning the speed was sufficient enough for communication service to work properly. Starlink
is crucial for Ukraine's military and defensive operations. This really matters, Zelensky said,
for our frontline logistics for defending Ukraine against jet-powered jet-head drones.
Last week, without warning, Ukraine lost the ability to use Starlink for these critical
functions. Even though now it's working again, the country is seeking for alternative satellite
communications not to rely only on American technology. Polina Litvinova, NPR News, Kyiv.
Remnants of Hurricane Trudy continue moving through the Four Corners region,
bringing with it flooding that's displaced residents there. Jamie Wanzek reports from Durango,
Colorado. As heavy rains in southern Colorado and northern New Mexico begin to recede,
dangerous flooding conditions remain in Farmington, New Mexico. Devin Neely is with San Juan County.
The water in both the San Juan and Anamis River is contaminated with raw sewage.
Folks need to stay out of the flood water, and there are some severe dangers associated
with the flood waters right now. Farmington Utilities has shut off power in areas inundated
with water. The National Guard continues to assist with local and state crews with aerial
and swift water rescues in much of northwest New Mexico and the Navajo Nation. For NPR News,
I'm Jamie Wanzek in Durango, Colorado. And this is NPR News.
An apparent explosion caused a fire at a Quaker Oats factory in Cedar Rapids, Iowa Saturday
afternoon. Mayor Tiffany O'Donnell says all the workers got out safely and there were no injuries.
The fire occurred in an area of the factory that had few employees. The cause of the fire
is unknown and under investigation. Six Flags says it will add secondary restraints on its
rides across the chain that are similar to the roller coaster Goliath at its Georgia park.
That's where a man died after he was thrown from his seat. Melissa Fato from member station WABE
reports. The seat belts similar to those worn in an airplane or car will be used in addition to the
coaster's mechanical restraints, the company says. Some Six Flags rides already use these type of
restraints. CEO John Riley did not specify which attractions will get seat belts, but eight other
rides of the hyper coaster and giga coaster models manufactured by the Swiss firm Bolliger and
Mabelard remain closed across the chain. Goliath also remains closed pending "necessary safety
reviews and clearances." Officials are still investigating what caused 42-year-old Hassan
Karim's death at Six Flags over Georgia. This is the first major change the company has announced
since the accident earlier this month. For NPR News, I'm Melissa Fato in Atlanta.
Cabbie Williams scored 17 points Saturday as Golden State beat the Atlanta dream 67-62 in
the WNBA Finals. The win ties the best of seven series at two games apiece. The Valkyries were
able to box in Atlanta star Angel Reiss holding her to just eight points. She's dominated the
previous two games averaging 25.5 points and 14 rebounds. This time she missed 10 of her 12 shots.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from IXL. The first few weeks back at school
set the tone for the rest of the year. IXL is designed to help kids build confidence and get
up to speed fast. Covering pre-k through 12th grade, IXL offers personalized interactive practice
in math, language arts, and science. One subscription covers everything for all the
kids in your home. Receive an exclusive 20% discount on an IXL membership at ixl.com/npr.

topics.text: Obama campaigns in Detroit and Ohio, blaming Trump policies for high consumer prices
Trump casts early ballot in Florida, then heads to Georgia; Audi announces $4.2 billion plant
Ukraine says Starlink is fully functioning again after disruption, seeks alternatives to US technology
Hurricane Trudy remnants bring flooding to Four Corners region, displacing residents in New Mexico
Apparent explosion sparks fire at Quaker Oats factory in Cedar Rapids, Iowa; no injuries
Six Flags adds seat belt restraints across its roller coasters after Georgia rider death on Goliath
Golden State beats Atlanta Dream 67-62 in WNBA Finals, evening series at two games apiece
